channel.title: The African Street Journal
channel.description: Daily news from all 55 African countries, every source cited.

item.title: UK deploys facial recognition for immigration crackdown
item.description: The United Kingdom plans to use live facial recognition technology at transport hubs and public events.

item.title: Female artisanal miners report sexual violence in Kono district
item.description: Women working in the diamond-rich pits of Jaiama Nimikor face persistent threats of rape and harassment while struggling to earn a daily income.

item.title: Sierra Leone charcoal burning causes deforestation
item.description: Environmental agency warns of economic tree loss and habitat destruction due to cooking fuel production.

item.title: Sierra Leone president warns kush drug peddlers
item.description: President Bio visits a rehabilitation center and urges immediate cessation of illicit drug trade.

item.title: Tanzania seeks AfDB funding for new power line
item.description: The government discussed financing for a 400kV transmission line from Kisongo to Segera with the African Development Bank.

item.title: Togo cyber unit warns of fake job scam
item.description: CERT.TG alerts citizens to social media recruitment drive using fake offers and suspicious links.

item.title: Eswatini coach attends ICC Level 2 course in Kenya
item.description: Mancoba Jele aims to train local cricket instructors after completing a four-day programme in Nairobi.

item.title: Namibia launches state-owned air ambulance service
item.description: The new service aims to reduce travel time for critically ill patients from remote areas to hospitals.

item.title: Dangote launches N$41.6 billion pipeline project in Walvis Bay
item.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote promises cheaper fuel for Namibia with a new N$41.6 billion pipeline project.

item.title: Ouattara, Macron discuss cooperation
item.description: The Ivorian and French presidents met for two hours at the Élysée Palace on November 3, 2026.

item.title: Malawi mines absent from Commonwealth investment plan
item.description: The Commonwealth Investment Platform lists 115 projects worth US$52.9bn but omits mining infrastructure.

item.title: Kano state to irrigate 2,000 acres for farming
item.description: 11 new mini dams will expand year-round cultivation, boosting farmer productivity and rural incomes.

item.title: Mauritius ranks second in African governance index
item.description: The nation maintains its strong institutional standing but sees a decline in its overall score over a decade.

item.title: Five arrested after customary conflict in Maï-Ndombe village
item.description: Police transferred five individuals to Mushie after clashes erupted in Mba village over a customary dispute.

item.title: Algerian study finds link between eye floaters and retinal tears
item.description: A study of 896 people found 9.9% with posterior vitreous detachment also had retinal tears.

item.title: Zimbabwe health ministry warns of heatstroke risk
item.description: The Ministry of Health and Child Care advises vigilance as forecasts predict hotter-than-normal temperatures for the 2026/2027 season.

item.title: Frelimo pledges funds for Maputo oncology unit repair
item.description: The ruling party announced a contribution to restore the hospital unit damaged by fire on Sunday.

item.title: Burundi families sell land for stroke treatment
item.description: Stroke patients' relatives face financial ruin and disrupted lives due to costly care.

item.title: Namibia road funding gap narrows to N$2.3 billion
item.description: Road Fund Administration adjusts user charges and seeks market borrowing to fund critical projects.

item.title: Ghana chamber seeks industry-wide financing collaboration
item.description: The Ghana Chamber of Clean Energy is pushing for joint efforts to overcome funding hurdles in the electric two-wheeler sector.

item.title: MSF warns 150,000 displaced face disease risk
item.description: Funding cuts threaten water, sanitation, and health services for people in Bentiu and Malakal camps.

item.title: South Sudan launches mobile courts to clear case backlog
item.description: The 30-day initiative in Western Bahr el Ghazal aims to speed up justice and reduce detention times.

item.title: Equatorial Guinea reviews Securiport border control fees
item.description: Vice President Nguema Obiang Mangue chairs meeting in Malabo to assess company's economic proposal.

item.title: MFA youth football league continues Saturday
item.description: The Mauritius Football Association's youth championships will feature U15 and U17 boys' matches across six grounds.

item.title: Windhoek starts utility disconnections for unpaid bills
item.description: Human rights lawyer Norman Tjombe questions the legality of cutting off water and electricity to residents and businesses with outstanding municipal accounts.

item.title: Rina’s Empower Her Foundation offers free breast cancer screening
item.description: Women in Freetown’s Mabela community received free breast cancer screening and education on symptoms.

item.title: Sheriff Barrie credits Momoh for 1991 constitution
item.description: National Democratic Alliance Acting Chairman Sheriff Barrie stated that former President Joseph Saidu Momoh initiated the constitutional process.

item.title: Tanzania opens applications for boxing commission leadership
item.description: The National Sports Council is accepting applications until November 17th for eight leadership positions within the TPBRC.

item.title: Tanzania strengthens food security efforts
item.description: Officials and stakeholders emphasize resilient food systems beyond just increasing crop production.

item.title: Dakar rally to pass through occupied Western Sahara
item.description: The race will traverse Smara and reach Dajla between January 18 and 22, crossing territory claimed by Morocco.

item.title: Hichilema visits Mandevu, election cancelled
item.description: President Hichilema will meet Mandevu residents today as all opposition candidates withdraw from the by-election.

item.title: Mozambique fuel retailers launch digital platform
item.description: ARCOMOC's new system connects operators nationwide to simplify information access and reduce bureaucracy.

item.title: Madagascar court allows constitutional referendum before presidential vote
item.description: The High Constitutional Court ruled that a referendum to adopt a new constitution can proceed before the presidential election.

item.title: Sergeant refuses to attend shooting inquiry reconstitution
item.description: Key witnesses recreated the events of October 9 when Elodie Thomas was shot.

item.title: Mali president attends Russia-Africa forum in Moscow
item.description: Discussions focused on technology transfer, food security, and youth training in Moscow on October 28, 2026.

item.title: Botswana women's football faces funding gap
item.description: The launch of a 20-team Women's National First Division is threatened by a lack of sponsorship and infrastructure.

item.title: Libyan publishers face rising book costs
item.description: Imported paper and fluctuating exchange rates drive up production expenses for local bookmakers.

item.title: Ghana, Trinidad and Tobago explore joint reparatory justice mechanism
item.description: Ministers discussed a dedicated platform, potentially co-chaired by AU and CARICOM, for engagement with the UK.

item.title: Malawi farmers need irrigation equipment
item.description: Nsanje District farmers can only cultivate half of their land due to a lack of water pumps.

item.title: Activist walks SA to protest farm attacks
item.description: Petrus Sitho left a job in 2018 to speak out about farm murders and has walked hundreds of kilometres.

item.title: Wetangula, Kingi lead MPs to visit recuperating Oburu
item.description: National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetangula and Senate Speaker Amason Kingi visited ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi home on November 5.

item.title: Ghana to build 21,000-tonne grain storage facility
item.description: The Ministry of Food and Agriculture signed an MoU with DMT Collateral Management for the facility in Wa, Upper West Region.

item.title: Mauritius tourism operators train for sustainable practices
item.description: The Tourism Authority and OIF are equipping hotels and guesthouses with tools for environmental and economic resilience.

item.title: Mozambique releases $50 million for fuel imports
item.description: Minister Estevão Pale announced measures to ease fuel supply constraints following international market disruptions.

item.title: Malawi state firms lose K640 billion
item.description: World Bank report highlights weak cash flows and declining dividends from government-owned enterprises.

item.title: Peter Obi visit prompts Bayelsa political shifts
item.description: Ijaw leaders demand development and unity following the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate's visit.

item.title: Naira trades at ₦1,347.30 in official market
item.description: The naira weakened for a second consecutive trading session, closing at N1,348 per dollar on Wednesday.

item.title: Burkina journalists trained on terrorism finance investigations
item.description: 30 journalists learned techniques for investigating illicit trafficking and funding of terrorism in Burkina Faso and the Sahel.

item.title: Namibia beef industry faces N$2.4 billion FMD loss
item.description: The foot-and-mouth disease outbreak threatens export access and processing investments, impacting jobs and households.

item.title: Seychelles backs Lana Nusseibeh for UN chief
item.description: The island nation supports the candidate in a race with seven contenders for the top UN position.

item.title: Seychelles parliament amends tobacco control law
item.description: Lawmakers voted unanimously to update the 2009 Tobacco Control Act for new products like vapes.

item.title: Roke Telkom marks 20 years of Ugandan ICT services
item.description: The telecommunications company celebrated its anniversary with the Uganda Communications Commission chief in attendance.

item.title: Algerian investor harvests apples 18 months after planting
item.description: Amine Derrar's 28-hectare farm in Tiaret yielded a good crop due to technical processes and irrigation.

item.title: Mauritius farmers get 257.9 hectares for climate adaptation
item.description: Minister Arvin Boolell announced land allocation and a new roadmap to address irrigation, pesticide use, and labor shortages.

item.title: Malawi mourns poet Jack Mapanje
item.description: The writer, known for exploring freedom and power, died in the United Kingdom.

item.title: Sudan demolishes over 100 homes in Al-Jazira village
item.description: Residents protest demolitions, citing discrimination and lack of shelter as winter approaches.

item.title: Malawi allows private power producers to feed grid
item.description: New net-metering rules let individuals and companies sell surplus renewable energy to the national grid.

item.title: Benin prefect tours N’Dali and Pèrèrè communes
item.description: Prefect Abdoul-Chakour Naro Assouma met local leaders to discuss security and infrastructure.

item.title: Cotonou mayor orders cemetery upkeep
item.description: Luc Gnacadja inspects PK 14, Zogbo, and Akpakpa cemeteries after three months of maintenance work.

item.title: Mahama defends speed cameras after child deaths
item.description: President Mahama says Ghana cannot delay stricter traffic enforcement as children continue to die on roads.

item.title: Madagascar parliament to review 2027 budget
item.description: The finance bill proposes 5.1% economic growth and targets energy, roads, agriculture, education, and health.

item.title: Madagascar taekwondo championships end in Fianarantsoa
item.description: 320 taekwondo athletes competed in combat and poomsae events over two days.

item.title: Mali military court hears eight cases
item.description: Accused include officers and civilians facing charges from desertion to fraud.

item.title: Eswatini farmers urged to sell livestock as drought kills over 50 cattle
item.description: Shiselweni Region faces severe water and pasture shortages, impacting livestock health and productivity.

item.title: Eswatini court hears explosive found in South Africa
item.description: Assistant Superintendent Bhekani Shiba testified that a device was collected from Bonginkhosi IB Dlamini’s home in South Africa.

item.title: Eswatini football squad announcement delayed
item.description: The Eswatini Football Association has failed to name the Sihlangu Semnikati team for a friendly against Malta.

item.title: Three Koumé family members face Nouakchott court
item.description: Family members arrested during a forced eviction on October 21 are to appear before the prosecutor on November 5.

item.title: US-funded vaccine trial cancelled in Guinea-Bissau
item.description: Accusations of unethical and neocolonial practices led to the cancellation of a hepatitis B vaccine trial on newborns.

item.title: Morocco cuts illegal cannabis cultivation by 88%
item.description: The Ministry of Interior reported a significant drop in cannabis farming areas from 134,000 hectares in 2003 to 15,496 hectares in 2026.

item.title: Meheba refugees face new gate pass rules
item.description: Camp officials announced gate passes will now take one week to issue and last three months.

item.title: Burundi engineer disappears, three SOSUMO officials questioned
item.description: Ismaël Mugisha, an engineer at the Moso Sugar Company, has been missing since October 30, prompting an investigation.

item.title: CRIEF summons officials in 3.135 tonnes gold case
item.description: Four personalities, including the current central bank governor, will testify on November 23 regarding alleged gold embezzlement.

item.title: Tunisian police seize cannabis and drugs in Sousse
item.description: Authorities arrested three dealers and confiscated approximately 250 grams of cannabis resin and psychotropic pills.

item.title: Senegal increases insulin subsidy to 520 million CFA francs
item.description: The Ministry of Health aims to promote annual health check-ups for all citizens to prevent costly diseases.

item.title: Germany funds 15 million euros for Mauritanian jobs
item.description: Nouakchott and Berlin sign financing agreement to support small and medium enterprises.

item.title: Ivory Coast trains rice processors to boost local quality
item.description: A four-day workshop in Yamoussoukro aims to improve milled rice quality and competitiveness against imports.

item.title: Mauritania affirms positive neutrality in regional affairs
item.description: Culture Minister Mohamed Ould Babana stated the nation is part of the solution, not the problem.

item.title: Chadian president meets Algerian minister
item.description: Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno and Ahmed Attaf discussed cooperation and regional security in N'Djamena.

item.title: Senegal launches national diabetes awareness campaign
item.description: The Association Sénégalaise de Soutien aux Diabétiques (ASSAD) is urging early screening and better management of the disease.

item.title: Morocco's dams fill as heavy rains hit north
item.description: National reservoirs hold 11.21 billion cubic meters of water, reaching 65.82% capacity after storms.

item.title: Stade Tunisien goalkeeper Nourddine Farhati repels attempts
item.description: The 26-year-old goalie turned away multiple attempts after conceding an early goal in a 2-1 victory.

item.title: Angolan court clarifies insult laws
item.description: The Folha 8 newspaper explains the legal distinction between slander, libel, and insult.

item.title: US proposes Sudan resource deal amid conflict
item.description: The Sudan IMPACT Act offers equipment and expertise for access to minerals and agriculture.

item.title: Mali hosts FMI delegation to discuss technical aid
item.description: The International Monetary Fund's West Africa technical assistance center director met with Mali's finance minister to identify aid needs.

item.title: Amad Diallo nominated for African Player of the Year
item.description: The Confederation of African Football revealed 10 nominees for the 2026 award, with the winner announced on December 7 in Lagos.

item.title: Kagame seeks Caribbean trade and investment partnerships
item.description: Rwandan president met leaders from four Caribbean nations on the sidelines of the Commonwealth summit.

item.title: Libya central bank governor takes legal oath
item.description: Fawzi Abu Khazam swore his oath before the House of Representatives to assume duties.

item.title: Chad security forces receive praise and equipment
item.description: Police officers in N'Djamena were recognized for arrests and dismantling a criminal network.

item.title: South Sudan NEC appoints election officials
item.description: Returning officers and assistants named for all 10 states and three administrative areas for December 2026 polls.

item.title: Guinea dismisses 22 officials over illegal gold mining
item.description: President Mamadi Doumbouya removed territorial administrators and officers for facilitating clandestine gold extraction.

item.title: Senegal futsal team wins first JOJ match
item.description: Mamadou Diagne scored the winning goal in the final minute against Panama.

item.title: Egypt targets 100,000 electric vehicles by 2032
item.description: Government plans to boost local manufacturing and reduce import dependence for automotive components.

item.title: Egypt seeks port integration with Slovenia
item.description: Cairo also wants a labour migration pact to send Egyptian workers to meet Slovenian demand.

item.title: Somalia rejects Israeli ambassador, embassy plan
item.description: Mogadishu declares Israel's moves in Somaliland a violation of sovereignty, null and void.

item.title: MP fears drought will leave patients hungry
item.description: Shiselweni I MP Shawnette Henwood questioned hospital preparedness for a potential El Niño drought and its impact on patient nutrition.

item.title: South Africans vote in local government elections
item.description: Voters cast ballots across Johannesburg on November 4, 2026, braving rain and queues.

item.title: Cape Verde police arrest 20 in drug trafficking sting
item.description: Operation Shark nets suspects including police and prison officers in Praia.

item.title: Raya Cyber Solutions debuts 45+ cybersecurity services in Egypt
item.description: The Raya IT subsidiary is showcasing its cybersecurity portfolio for the first time at Cairo ICT 2026.

item.title: Uganda agricultural body seeks private partnerships
item.description: NARO plans to commercialise research facilities like processing plants and mills to boost revenue.

item.title: Uganda Development Bank commits UGX 200 million to COP31
item.description: The bank will sponsor the Ugandan Pavilion for the second year, aiming to boost climate action and attract investment.
